Name: Charles Spurgeon
Summary: London's 'Prince of Preachers,' whose Metropolitan Tabernacle drew thousands weekly. Converted as a teenager in a snowstorm, he preached Christ-centered sermons, founded an orphanage and pastors' college, and printed sermons read worldwide.
Contribution: Modeled expository, Christ-centered preaching and combined evangelism with orphan care and ministry training.
Testimony: His testimony was simple: a boy who looked to Christ and lived, then spent fifty years pointing others to the same look.
